notes.title: NEW Summer 22 Demo!
notes.content:
Following extensive play-testing, Wreck Out is back with improved controls, better onboarding and revamped VFX. Try it now and tell us what you think!

All New VFX
Our suite of new visual effects makes the action more electrifying than ever. We've got new tackle particle systems, skid-marks, explosions and more.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/519f892b63aa43402a1e98a81ec83ccd73192dbf.jpg

Improve Controls
Wreck Out is now easier to pick-up-and-play than ever before. You are no longer required to swing the ball to shoot, just fire from-the-hip whenever you are ready. Experts can still pull of a devastating power-shot, but newcomers will find it easier to get up to speed.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/612495a33800024f035d19837f3a11fd3ac76099.jpg

We've also tweaked the tutorials, simplified the menus and added a work-in-progress tournament system against bots.

Enjoy, and let us know what you think.

notes.title: Power-Ups and Ultimates Updated
notes.content:
Following community feedback from recent playtesting events, we have overhauled the power-up system and the ultimate system to make them more simple, clear and effective. Let's take a look:

Ultimate Abilities
The system for ultimate abilities had been simplified as follows:

Assignment

BEFORE: The were randomly assigned to characters
NOW: Each character has a specific ultimate


Triggering

BEFORE: Play skillfully to fill your skill meter to level 1, 2 or 3 and then trigger
NOW: You can use your character's ultimate once per match


Ability Types

BEFORE: A mixture of ability types, from turning your opponent into an ice cube, to repelling tackles, to rebuilding or armouring bricks.
NOW: Ultimates always enhance your shooting or tackling capability i.e. they apply a super power to your existing capabilities.


Below you can see an example of the new Ignite Scattershot ultimate assigned to the Ignite character:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/dbf9232910e9c589c34a5f2a2a2cb676f9b92201.png

Power Ups
Power-ups are spawned from smashed bricks and can be collected during gameplay. The system has been updated as follows:

Collection

BEFORE: You could collect them by driving through them, or they could be collected by a loose ball, with the last player to have possession of the ball getting the power-up. This could sometimes be confusing as the frantic nature of the gameplay made it difficult to tell who has last touched the ball.
NOW: You can collect them by driving through them, but a loose ball will collide with them and push them around the arena. This means you can flush a power-up out of the loop in Pinball Dream Park for example by firing the ball through it.


Power-Up Types

BEFORE: We had one type of power-up which would randomly result in either bricks being rebuilt, armoured or shielded.
NOW: We now have separate power-ups for brick rebuild, armour and shield so you can clearly see the result before collecting.


These changes create an elegantly balanced system where Ultimates, which are offensive/attacking in nature, are character based and can be triggered once per match, while power-ups, which are defensive in nature, can be collected during gameplay.

notes.title: Art Style Overhaul 3/3
notes.content:
With new out-of-this-world arenas and party-time characters created, we needed a new-look logo for Wreckout to capture the essence of the game.

Capturing the Action
We wanted a logo which captured the unique action of Wreckout at a glance. We started with some concept sketches:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/19df1e345ecb67af4ee918be1245e71d4c6cd53f.png

We chose the sketch which felt like it captured the fun-factor of the game and the vehicle element, but we also wanted to incorporate the unique "car-catapult" mechanic which is central the the Wreckout experience, so the next stage was to sketch in some ideas for incorporating the tethered ball:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/304a46529dac0093acd251d72d0489ec60f5a782.png

We realised at this stage that we could capture another key element of the gameplay by using the font to represent the bricks which players smash up in the game. This was worked into the design as we moved into the colour-test phase:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/44d007edffc2b05d01902a819b57c711576c9111.png

With our colour-scheme chosen, we iterated on the ball tether and the bricks-smashing effect of the font, before producing the final render:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/52602dbc9b3b023f0e8529dc4f792b29273613f1.png

Finally, we combined it with the new arena and character artwork to complete the exciting new look for Wreckout!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/60ff0b36f3523d9950ba80dd792bb33e3db8c7cc.png

notes.title: Art Style Overhaul 2/3
notes.content:
We are excited to reveal the all-new art style for Wreckout - injecting the game with more colour, more character, and more action!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/7c706471c004c509312a2c8320e12721f3a09ecb.png

In our previous update we walked you through the development of the new Pinball Dream Park arena, now we'd like to show you how the all-new Wreckout characters were created.

Party-time Character
For the new-look characters, we've dialled up the cuteness, the coolness and the colour to create a diverse cast who are ready to compete and primed to party. Here's how the first two character for this new look were developed:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/d7eca587c2aa90b5146fa341b7d0d1339453420d.jpg

The first stage was simple sketches of different character ideas. We pulled out a bunch of references images for the style we had in mind, and the above sketches were produced.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/36bd2e15caacf2ab55abed105b0d4a087e8ee5f2.png

Next were some more sketches of male and female variants of the character which we found most appealing.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/39870044b797faa878a8ffdedd74345859238c6a.png

Then we tried out a few vehicle ideas for the characters. For gameplay reasons, the vehicles need to be square-shaped. This is because they can turn instantly in any direction for maximum manoeuvrability. A longer vehicle design looks awkward when turning on the spot, so the square shape had to be maintained. As a result, vehicle A was the style we moved forward with.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/00f24aac7a3cd506cd05afddf42ecce467c79720.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/a662fc5f1013a8ef70717c29385ad61e87076bdd.png 

More detailed sketches of the characters were then produced. You can see the grid lines beneath the car to ensure the vehicle is square shaped.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/654b5a4d2538ea225567e48b06381cf01a642871.png

Then it was on to the colour test stage, to determine the how the characters would look with a lick of paint.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/fc19bcc90016f29b378e87c781212d4ffef29a42.png

Finally, the characters were rendered off and animated to give us a polished result.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/ef035282407523499ccdf57b76786860923c675a.png

Only after the final character renders were produced was attention turned to producing the in-game vehicles to match, complete with rotating wheels and characters who could lean into turns.

notes.title: Art Style Overhaul 1/3
notes.content:
We are excited to reveal the all-new art style for Wreckout - injecting the game with more colour, more character, and more action!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/7c706471c004c509312a2c8320e12721f3a09ecb.png

We have already updated the store page assets with this vibrant new style, but we wanted to provide a behind-the-scenes look at the development process of the new arena, logo and characters.

Pinball Dream Park
Our renewed vision for the arenas in Wreckout is for each to embody an out-of-this-world theme, which spills over into gameplay. We started designing Pinball Dream Park by focusing on how a Pinball theme might affect gameplay in interesting ways. The first stage was to draw these elements over a screen-grab of the existing arena:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/c1fc216ba90b8915b64ed42ac341f197a9438853.png

A series of sketches were then produced to nail down the general style of the arena. From the thumbnails below, 3B was chosen:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/b33ff899041a32360083dad8078c89b572503666.png

A detailed sketch was then produced to fine-tune the design:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/317da2fa01704779ad9a0175c3162d1ef75c3b2b.png

Next, a colour draft was created to give a feeling of the new vibrant art style we were going for:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/86d4a890cd1433f4d17a875fc68ec940dec7c3e7.png

The final stage was a high-quality render, complete with multiple code-controllable lighting layers to allow spectacular in-game effects:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35779541/579e93402323bdf022227697308cfcce501d8728.png

We couldn't be happier with how Pinball Dream Park looks, and with flippers, bouncers, chutes and extra-ball launchers integrated into the design, it not only looks stunning, it also injects the gameplay with a whole new level of thrilling action.

notes.title: Wreckout Demo Guide - Steam Game Festival
notes.content:
Local and Online Multiplayer, 2-4 players
The Wreckout demo features both local multiplayer (2-4 players) and online multiplayer (2 players). Select "Find Game" in the online battle section and you will either join an existing lobby or begin hosting a game while you wait for a second player.

Coin Chase Practice Mode
There is also a single player practice mode where you can hone your skills while trying to collect as many coins as possible.

Controls
We recommend playing with a controller:
https://i.ibb.co/Qv51Wx9/controls.png

Hints & Tips
Like the best sports the basic rules of Wreckout are simple - whoever has the most bricks left at the end of each round wins - but there's a huge amount of depth and skill to master.

Rounds & Sudden Death
There are three rounds in a Wreckout match, like in a beat 'em up. If the score is equal at the end of a round you will enter "sudden death" where the next brick wins.
[previewyoutube=OS4pT39EecE;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Power Shot
Release the ball at just the right moment to do extra damage:
[previewyoutube=e3fCVfxHrr0;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Wrecking Ball Limiter
If you hold on to the ball and hit breaks, your energy beam will weaken until you drop the ball:
[previewyoutube=gEf_ODmG6xw;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Missing can backfire
If you miss your opponents bricks, the ball will bounce back more quickly, putting you on the defensive:
[previewyoutube=b1cZnGO9gXs;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Skill Meter & Ultimates
When you fill your skill meter to level 1, you can trigger your ultimate ability, but let it fill to level 3 and you will get triple the impact.

notes.title: Round System Explained
notes.content:
There are 3 rounds in a Wreckout match, like in a beat 'em up 🥊, but each round goes to sudden death ⚽️ if there's no winner when time runs out ⏱️.

[previewyoutube=OS4pT39EecE;full][/previewyoutube]

This system creates maximum drama, and breaks up matches into bite sized chunks. It also means there is always a winner and multiple different levels of victory, because each round can be won in three ways:

 Perfect: The winner destroys all of their opponents bricks before the timer runs down
 Timed: Both teams have one or more bricks remaining when the timer runs down, but the winner has more remaining
 Sudden Death: Both teams have an equal number of bricks remaining when the timer runs down, leading to “sudden death” where the next team to lose a brick loses the round.


Our plan is to then calculate a points value for the winner as follows:

Round 1: 3 points for Perfect, 2 for Timed and 1 for Sudden Death
Rounds 2/3: 5 points for Perfect, 3 for Timed and 1 for Sudden Death

So if you win, you get a minimum of 2 points and a maximum of 8 points depending on how dominant your victory was.

What do you think? Let us know is the comments.
